chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I entered upon al-Rida عليه السلام while, at that time, I was a Waqifi. My father had asked his father about seven questions, and he answered him concerning six and withheld from the seventh. So I said: “By Allah, I will surely ask him about what my father asked his father; if he answers with the same answer as his father, that will be a proof.” So I asked him, and he answered with the same answer as his father had answered my father regarding the six questions. He did not add to the answer a waw nor a ya, and he withheld from the seventh.

And my father had said to his father: “I will contend against you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection that you claimed that Abdullah was not an Imam.” So he placed his hand on his neck, then said to him: “Yes, contend against me with that before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whatever sin there may be in it is upon my neck.”

Then when I bade him farewell, he said: “There is no one among our Shi'a who is afflicted with an affliction or suffers a complaint and is patient upon that, except that Allah writes for him the reward of a thousand martyrs.” So I said to myself: “By Allah, there had been no mention of this.”

Then when I went on and was on part of the road, the vein of al-Madini came out in me, and I suffered severe pain from it. Then the following year I performed hajj and entered upon him while some of my pain still remained. I complained to him and said: “May I be made your ransom, seek refuge for my leg,” and I stretched it out before him. He said to me: “There is no harm in this leg of yours, but show me your sound leg.” So I stretched it out before him, and he sought refuge for it. Then when I went out, it was only a short while before the vein came out in me, and its pain was slight.

key_terms.أَجْرَ أَلْفِ شَهِيدٍ: The reward of a thousand martyrs granted for patient endurance
key_terms.بَلِيَّةٍ: An affliction or trial that befalls a person
key_terms.دَلَالَةً: A proof or indication establishing the truth of the matter
key_terms.عَوِّذْ: Seek protection or refuge for, meaning to recite for protection and healing
key_terms.وَاقِفِيٌّ: A follower of the Waqifi position at that time
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection when people are held to account before Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith present a proof for the Imamate of Imam al-Rida عليه السلام and the reward for patience in affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid found a proof of the Imamate of Imam al-Rida عليه السلام through his exact correspondence with the answers of his father. It also includes a statement about the immense reward of patience during affliction for the Shi'a, and a narrated instance of the Imam's seeking refuge for healing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, or someone else, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I went over to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, and I, in those days, was a Waqifiite, and it was so that my father had asked his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> about seven questions and he<sup>asws</sup> hand answered six and withheld from the seventh. So I said (to myself), ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I shall ask him<sup>asws</sup> about what my father asked his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>. So if he<sup>asws</sup> were to answer with the like of the answer of his<sup>asws</sup> father, it would be proof’. So I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> answered with like the answer of his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> to my father regarding the six questions, and he<sup>asws</sup> did not increase in the answer with neither a (letter) ‘Waw’ nor a (letter) ‘Ya’, and he<sup>asws</sup> withheld from the seventh.

And my father had said to his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I shall argue against you<sup>asws</sup> in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> on the Day of Judgment. You<sup>asws</sup> are claiming that Abdullah does not happen to be the Imam’. So he<sup>asws</sup> had placed his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon his neck, then said to him: ‘Yes, argue against me<sup>asws</sup> with that on the Day of Judgment in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic. So whatever was in it from a sin, so it would be upon my<sup>asws</sup> neck.

So when I bade him<sup>asws</sup> farewell, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There isn’t anyone from our<sup>asws</sup> Shias who is afflicted with an affliction or a complaint, so he is patient upon that, except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write to him the Recompense of a thousand martyrs’. So I said within myself, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! There was no mention of this’.

So when I went and was in one of the streets, a leg vein came out with me (swelled) and I faced intense (pain) from it. So when it was from the next year, I performed Hajj, and I went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and there had (still) remained some pain from my pains. So I complained to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! My leg is hurting’ and I extended it in front of him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘There is nothing wrong upon this leg of yours, but show me<sup>asws</sup> your correct leg’. So I extended it in front of him<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> sought Refuge (with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>) for it. So when I left, I did not wait except for a little while until the vein swelled with me, and it was of a little pain’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or a person other than him from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following.

“Once I went to see Ali al-Rida (a.s.). At that time I was a memebr of Waqifi sect. My father had asked his (al-Rida’s) father seven questions. He had replied to six of them and had refrained from answering the seventh. I said to my self, “By Allah, I will ask him what my father had asked his father if his answers will like those of his father it will serve as a good proof. I asked him those questions and hiis answers were just like the answers of his father to my father in the six questions. He did answer any more questions beyond six even not a letter ‘waw’ or letter ‘ya’’ and refrained from answering the seventh question.

My father had said to his father, “I will debate you before Allah on the Day of Judgment for your belief that ‘Abdallah is not an Imam. He then had placed his hand over my father’s neck and said, ““Yes, you may debate me about it before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious. If there will any sins in it will be on my neck.”

When I said farewell to him he said, “Whoever of our Shi‘a would suffer from any kind of afflictions or complains and he bears it patiently, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, will record for an entitlement to a reward equal to the rewards of a thousand martyrs.” I then said to my self, “By Allah, there was no mention of this (in our conversations).”

I then left and on the way a vein in my began to feel very soar and the pain intensified. Next year when I went for Hajj I went to see the him. My leg was still slightly painful. I complained before him of the pain and requested him to say a prayer on it and I stretched it before him.” He said, “There is nothing wrong with this leg but show me your leg that is not ill. I then stretched it before him and he said a prayer. When I left little later on my leg began to feel the pain in a vein but it was very little.”
